entry.title: Noticing what belongs together
entry.summary: Davies describes toddlers grouping things by type, color, or size from around 18 months. The interest in likeness is the starting point, with an adult supervising small materials.
entry.cue: Notice your child bringing similar things together or sorting clothes during an ordinary task.
detail: The chapter proposes a group of objects and bowls or a divided container. The appendix gives two kinds of an item as a simple comparison. Your child can explore the differences without being quizzed for the right answer.

The small-button photograph is labeled from 2 years, later than the broader sorting discussion. It does not set the materials for every 18-month-old. Sorting socks or clothing is also part of the book’s household participation examples.
